'''The Main Event''' took place, and aired live, on Friday February 5, 1988 at 8pm ET at [[Market Square Arena]] in [[Indianapolis, Indiana]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.onlineworldofwrestling.com/results/snme/880205.html |title=Online World of Wrestling |publisher=Online World of Wrestling |date=1988-02-05 |access-date=2012-03-04}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=The Main Event: February 5, 1988| publisher=World Wrestling Entertainment| url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/snme/history/1985to1992/feb051988| access-date=2015-08-28}}</ref> The live broadcast drew a 15.2 [[Nielsen rating]] and 33 million viewers, both records for American televised wrestling.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://slam.canoe.com/Slam/Wrestling/Wrestlemania20/WrestleMania3.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150429201526/http://slam.canoe.com/Slam/Wrestling/Wrestlemania20/WrestleMania3.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 29, 2015|title=Steamboat&nbsp;— Savage rule WrestleMania 3|last=Powell|first=John|publisher=SLAM! Wrestling|access-date=October 14, 2007}}</ref>

The match between [[André the Giant]] and [[Hulk Hogan]] saw André receive a [[pinfall]] victory despite Hogan raising his left shoulder before a count of two could be reached. It was revealed, post-match, that the referee who worked the match was not the assigned referee, [[Dave Hebner]], but rather his twin brother, [[Earl Hebner]].  Earl had been hired by [[Ted DiBiase]] to cheat Hogan out of the belt.  Immediately after the match, André surrendered the title to DiBiase.  Later on, WWF President [[Jack Tunney]] said the title can only change hands by pinfall or submission.  Tunney acknowledged that the referee's decision is final but, due to André surrendering the belt, he declared the title to be vacant.<ref name=wwechamp>{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/inside/titlehistory/wwechampionship/304454122 |title=Andre the Giant's first reign |website=[[WWE]] | access-date=February 15, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050624001310/http://www.wwe.com/inside/titlehistory/wwechampionship/304454122 |archive-date=June 24, 2005}}</ref> Following the vacancy, a single elimination tournament was held at [[WrestleMania IV]] to crown the new champion.<ref>{{Cite web |title=WrestleMania IV |author=Puckering, Dean |work=TWM Wrestling News |access-date=March 19, 2019 |url=http://www.twm.news/wrestlemania-iv/ }}</ref>

The [[Strike Force (professional wrestling)|Strike Force]] vs. [[The Hart Foundation]] match was still in progress when NBC signed off. In 2014, when the [[WWE Network]] made available this episode to its on-demand section, the ending of the match was added in.

===The Main Event II===

'''The Main Event II''' took place and aired live on Friday February 3, 1989 at 8pm ET from the [[Bradley Center]] in [[Milwaukee|Milwaukee, Wisconsin]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.onlineworldofwrestling.com/results/snme/890203.html |title=Online World of Wrestling |publisher=Online World of Wrestling |date=1989-02-03 |access-date=2012-03-04}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=The Main Event: February 3, 1989|publisher=World Wrestling Entertainment|url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/snme/history/1985to1992/feb031989|access-date=2015-08-28}}</ref> The live broadcast drew an 11.6 rating and 19.9 million viewers.<ref>{{cite news |date=February 8, 1989 |title=Nielsen ratings |work=[[USA Today]] |page=3D |id={{ProQuest|306179902}}}}</ref>

The slowly building tension between [[Hulk Hogan]] and [["Macho Man" Randy Savage]] boiled over during the team's match against [[The Twin Towers (professional wrestling)|The Twin Towers]], leading to the team's breakup upon Savage's heel turn when Savage contended that Hogan was lusting after his manager, [[Miss Elizabeth]].{{citation needed|date=September 2019}}
